It's a music genre/culture that started and rose in Seattle in the 80s/90s. It peaked in popularity, the 90s, with such bands as Nirvana, Stone Temple Pilots and Pearl Jam.
I remember it as a refreshing and genuine if short lived and musically shallow, opposition movement to and a counter-point and reaction to the sterility of the sound and image of 80s pop culture.

It's just a catch all term for many of the a lot of the rock bands of the late '80s, early 90's. I get that the Seattle scene had a huge role in the term becoming widely used, but I agree with u/Greenseats. Those bands all sounded very much different. And the ones that stayed around experimented and evolved their music in ways that wouldn't necessarily fit with what the general population would consider grunge music, as u/kiwikoi pointed out. I think it's more defined by a time and place, certain bands, than a sound. Play some Dead Kennedys and people will tell you it's punk. Put on Slayer and people will tell you it's thrash metal. But play anything from from the grunge era and you may or may not have someone call it grunge.
I don't know exactly what it is, but it's the music I love, it's the music I feel, it's the music that speaks to me.
